result:
Here's the chain, from spec to code to failure behavior.

**What the screen spec claims.** The feature-flags screen is documented as SCR-022 in `docs/ui/screen-settings-billing-flags-webhooks.md`, at route `/{orgSlug}/settings/flags`, backed by `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/page.tsx` and `flag-toggle-list.tsx`. Its metadata block states: **"Permission required: `org:manage_flags` (member and above) — 404 otherwise."**

**What the requirement and design docs say the permission actually is.** `docs/requirements/feature-flags.md` (REQ-192, "toggling a flag requires admin") and `docs/design/service-feature-flag-and-support.md` both describe `org:manage_flags` as an `admin`-minimum permission, tied to `toggleFlag` in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts`. This is echoed independently in `docs/requirements/membership-and-roles.md` (REQ-024, "Admins manage membership, flags and archiving") and in `docs/design/permission-model.md`, which walks through `ROLE_MATRIX` and lists `org:manage_flags` alongside `member:invite`, `org:update`, `project:archive`, etc. as `admin`-minimum actions. All of these agree with each other, and disagree with the screen spec's "member and above."

**Where the decision is actually made in code.** `src/lib/permissions.ts` defines `ROLE_MATRIX`, and its entry is `"org:manage_flags": "admin"` — not `member`. The single authorization entry point is `can()` (with `explain()` as its reasoned twin), and per ADR-003 (`docs/adr/ADR-003-single-permission-entry-point.md`) every authorization check in the codebase must funnel through it. Its decision order, also documented in `permission-model.md`, is: cross-tenant guard (`assertOrgScope`-style check that actor.orgId matches the resource's orgId) → platform-staff bypass (`actor.isPlatformStaff`) → role-matrix rank comparison (`ROLE_RANK[actor.role] >= ROLE_RANK[ROLE_MATRIX[action]]`) → ownership escalation. `org:manage_flags` is not one of the five actions in the ownership-escalation set (`issue:update`, `issue:archive`, `comment:update`, `comment:delete`, `notification:manage`), so for this permission the decision resolves purely on the role-matrix branch: `granted_by_role` if the actor's rank is `admin` or `owner`, `denied_by_role` otherwise.

Concretely, in `page.tsx` the page loads tenant context via `loadTenantContext(orgSlug)`, then calls `can(actor, "org:manage_flags", { kind: "organization", orgId: org.id })`. Because `ROLE_MATRIX["org:manage_flags"]` is `"admin"`, a `member`-role actor fails this check even though the screen spec says they shouldn't. The mutation path enforces the same gate a second time: `toggleFeatureFlagAction` (`src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts`) calls into `feature-flag-service.ts`'s `toggleFlag`, which checks `org:manage_flags` again before touching the flag registry — so even if a `member` somehow reached the page, the server action would still refuse the toggle.

**What happens to a user who fails the check.** The page does not render a "no access" message. If `can()` returns false, `page.tsx` calls Next.js's `notFound()` immediately (`if (!allowed) { notFound(); }`), which renders the app's generic 404 (`src/app/not-found.tsx`). This matches the documented Taskflow convention in `docs/ui/index.md`: "permission denied" resolves to a bare 404 rather than an explanatory message, specifically so a caller without the permission can't infer the route exists at all.

**Does the spec's stated minimum match the code?** No. The screen spec (SCR-022) says `org:manage_flags` is "member and above," but the actual `ROLE_MATRIX` entry in `src/lib/permissions.ts`, corroborated by the requirements doc (REQ-192/REQ-024), the design doc, and the service implementation (`toggleFlag`), is `admin`. The screen spec is out of sync with the code and with the rest of the documentation — a `member`-role actor visiting `/{orgSlug}/settings/flags` will get a 404, contrary to what the spec's metadata block implies.
